outcome: Developmental delay (overall, gross motor, fine motor, and language)
cohort: 178,235 children aged 1-36 months who had a routine physical examination in hospitals across 16 provinces, 4 autonomous regions, and 2 municipalities directly under the central government in China from March 2018 to November 2021
finding: Perinatal factors, including male sex, parity, advanced maternal age, multiple birth, cesarean section, neonatal injury, family history of developmental delay, microcephaly, and abnormal BMI at birth and at physical examination, were significantly associated with developmental delay in Chinese children aged 1-36 months.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was found to be a significant risk factor for developmental delay.
